title: The Ledger in the Woods
subject: SQL
intro: Mira's archive records every trade made in the woods. Ask the database which product brings in the most money, using real SQL queries.

objectives.label: Read what a SELECT query asks for
Group rows and add them up with GROUP BY and SUM
Find the top result with ORDER BY and LIMIT
Say only what the data supports

badge.name: Ledger Reader
badge.description: Asked a database real questions and checked what the answer meant.

takeaway: A database answers exactly the question you write. SELECT picks columns, WHERE picks rows, GROUP BY with SUM adds things up, and ORDER BY with LIMIT finds the top result. Then you still decide what the answer does and doesn't prove.

scenes.title: The archive cellar
scenes.speaker: mira
lines: Welcome back, Pathfinder. Down here is the ledger: every lantern, map and compass sold across the island.
The village council wants to know which product earns the most. Adding it up by hand would take all night.
Instead, we'll ask the database. It speaks a language called SQL. Let's learn a few words of it.

scenes.title: Reading a query
scenes.speaker: mira
scenes.context: Every SQL question starts the same way. Here is a simple one.
scenes.prompt: What does this query ask the database to do?

options.text: Show the product and revenue columns for every row in the sales table
options.feedback: Yes. SELECT lists the columns you want; FROM names the table. With nothing else, you get every row.

options.text: Remove the product and revenue columns from the table
options.feedback: SELECT only reads. It never changes or deletes data.

options.text: Sort the sales table by product and revenue
options.feedback: Sorting needs ORDER BY. This query just picks which columns to show.
Adding up needs SUM(). This query shows the revenue of each row individually.

hints: Read it like a sentence: SELECT these columns FROM this table.
Nothing in the query says delete, sort or total.
scenes.explanation: SELECT chooses which columns appear in the result; FROM says which table to read. A query on its own never changes the data.

scenes.title: Only the North
scenes.speaker: mira
scenes.context: The council asked about the North region first.
scenes.prompt: Write a query that shows the product and revenue of sales in the North region only.
scenes.setup: CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, product TEXT, region TEXT, units INTEGER, revenue INTEGER); INSERT INTO sales VALUES (1,'Lantern','North',12,240),(2,'Map','North',8,160),(3,'Compass','South',5,175),(4,'Lantern','South',20,400),(5,'Map','East',15,300),(6,'Compass','North',9,315),(7,'Lantern','East',30,600),(8,'Map','South',4,80);
scenes.successFeedback: Three North sales, exactly as in the table.
hints: Add a WHERE line after FROM sales to keep only some rows.
Text values go in single quotes: WHERE region = 'North'
scenes.explanation: WHERE keeps only the rows that match a condition. Text must be in quotes, and the spelling must match the data exactly.

scenes.title: Add it up
scenes.speaker: mira
scenes.context: Now the whole island. Each product appears in several rows, so we need to group them.
scenes.prompt: Write a query that shows each product once, with its total revenue.
scenes.setup: CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, product TEXT, region TEXT, units INTEGER, revenue INTEGER); INSERT INTO sales VALUES (1,'Lantern','North',12,240),(2,'Map','North',8,160),(3,'Compass','South',5,175),(4,'Lantern','South',20,400),(5,'Map','East',15,300),(6,'Compass','North',9,315),(7,'Lantern','East',30,600),(8,'Map','South',4,80);
scenes.starter:
SELECT product, SUM(revenue) AS total
FROM sales
scenes.successFeedback: One row per product, each with its total.
hints: SUM(revenue) adds values up, but it needs to know how to split the rows. That's GROUP BY.
Finish the starter with: GROUP BY product
scenes.explanation: GROUP BY collects rows that share a value into one group; SUM() then adds up each group. Together they turn many rows into one summary row per product.

scenes.title: The top earner
scenes.speaker: mira
scenes.context: One last question for the ledger: which product is on top?
scenes.prompt: Write a query that returns only the single product with the highest total revenue, and that total.
scenes.setup: CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, product TEXT, region TEXT, units INTEGER, revenue INTEGER); INSERT INTO sales VALUES (1,'Lantern','North',12,240),(2,'Map','North',8,160),(3,'Compass','South',5,175),(4,'Lantern','South',20,400),(5,'Map','East',15,300),(6,'Compass','North',9,315),(7,'Lantern','East',30,600),(8,'Map','South',4,80);
scenes.starter:
SELECT product, SUM(revenue) AS total
FROM sales
GROUP BY product
scenes.solution:
SELECT product, SUM(revenue) AS total
FROM sales
GROUP BY product
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 1;
hints: Sort the grouped results from highest to lowest with ORDER BY … DESC.
Then keep just the first row with LIMIT 1.
scenes.explanation: ORDER BY total DESC puts the biggest total first, and LIMIT 1 keeps only that row. Sorting and limiting is the everyday way to find a top result.

scenes.title: What can we tell the council?
scenes.speaker: mira
scenes.context: The query says Lanterns earned 1240, the highest total in the ledger.
scenes.prompt: Which statement can you safely make to the council?

options.text: Lanterns brought in the most revenue in these records
options.feedback: Yes. That's exactly what the query measured, nothing more.

options.text: Lanterns are our most profitable product
options.feedback: Profit needs costs, and the ledger has none. High revenue can still mean low profit.

options.text: Lanterns will sell the most next year too
options.feedback: The ledger describes the past. It can't promise the future.
Lowest revenue alone isn't enough to decide that. Compasses might be cheap to make, or bring customers in.

hints: Which columns did your query actually use?
Revenue is money coming in. Does the table say anything about costs or next year?
scenes.explanation: A query answers the question it asked. Revenue isn't profit, and past sales aren't a forecast. Saying exactly what the data shows keeps your analysis trustworthy.

scenes.title: The ledger speaks
scenes.speaker: mira
lines: A whole night's adding up, done in four short questions. The council will be delighted.
And you were careful to say only what the numbers show. That's the habit that matters most.
The traders at the market keep their books in spreadsheets. They could use a Pathfinder too.
